input.task: Write the investment thesis and the recommendation on CISCO SYSTEMS, INC. (CSCO) from the two analysts' outputs.

overview.claim: Cisco designs and sells hardware, software and AI-powered digital infrastructure that powers, helps secure and draws insights from the Internet.
overview.quote: Cisco designs and sells a broad range of technologies including hardware, software, and artificial intelligence (AI) powered digital infrastructure to power, help secure, and draw insights from the Internet.

overview.claim: Cisco earns money from product sales and from services over the life of those products, including technical support and professional services.
overview.quote: In addition to our product offerings, we provide a broad range of services over the lifecycle of our products, including technical support services and professional services.

overview.claim: Product revenue grew 16% while services revenue was flat.
overview.quote: Within total revenue, product revenue increased by 16% and services revenue was flat.

business_model.claim: Cisco manages its business through three geographic segments: Americas, EMEA and APJC.
business_model.quote: Our business is organized into the following three geographic segments: Americas; Europe, Middle East, and Africa (EMEA); and Asia Pacific, Japan, and China (APJC).

business_model.claim: Cisco's customers operate mainly in the enterprise, public sector, and service provider and cloud markets.
business_model.quote: Our customers primarily operate in the following markets: enterprise, public sector and service provider and cloud.

business_model.claim: Cisco sells a substantial portion of its products and services through channel partners and the remainder through direct sales.
business_model.quote: A substantial portion of our products and services is sold indirectly through channel partners, and the remainder is sold through direct sales.

business_model.claim: Networking is the largest product category, with product revenue of $34,668 million, up 22%.

competitive_position.claim: Cisco's total revenue reached $63.3 billion, up 12% compared with fiscal 2025.
competitive_position.quote: Total revenue was $63.3 billion, an increase of 12% compared with fiscal 2025.

competitive_position.claim: Cisco's high-performance systems run mainly on its own Cisco Silicon One architecture, which covers all AI networking roles.
competitive_position.quote: Our high-performance systems are predominantly powered by Cisco Silicon One, a scalable and programmable architecture, covering all AI networking roles and capable of adapting to a wide range of use cases and network infrastructure designs.

competitive_position.claim: The filing names competitors including Amazon Web Services, Arista Networks, Broadcom, Huawei, Microsoft, Nvidia, Palo Alto Networks and Zscaler.
competitive_position.quote: Our competitors (in each case relative to only some of our products or services) include: Amazon Web Services LLC; Arista Networks, Inc.; Broadcom Inc.; Ciena Corporation; CrowdStrike Holdings, Inc.; Datadog Inc.; Dell Technologies Inc.; Dynatrace Inc.; Fortinet, Inc.; Hewlett-Packard Enterprise Company; Huawei Technologies Co., Ltd.; Microsoft Corporation; Nokia Corporation; Nvidia Corporation; Palo Alto Networks, Inc.; RingCentral, Inc.; Zoom Video Communications, Inc.; and Zscaler, Inc.; among others.

competitive_position.claim: Cisco faces price-focused competition from Asian competitors, especially from China, and expects it to continue.
competitive_position.quote: In particular, we have experienced price-focused competition from competitors in Asia, especially from China, and we anticipate this will continue.

catalysts.claim: Management expects hyperscaler demand for AI infrastructure to remain a significant driver of results in fiscal 2027.
catalysts.quote: We expect this demand to remain a significant driver of our results in fiscal 2027, and we discuss the associated customer concentration and supply considerations in Part I, Item 1A. Risk Factors.

catalysts.claim: Cisco raised its expectation for AI infrastructure revenue from hyperscalers to $9B in FY27, more than double the FY26 total.
catalysts.quote: •Raised expectation for AI infrastructure revenue from hyperscalers to $9B in FY27, more than double the total for FY26

catalysts.claim: Cisco announced a restructuring plan to invest in key growth opportunities including silicon, optics, security and AI.
catalysts.quote: In the fourth quarter of fiscal 2026, we announced a restructuring plan to allow us to invest in key growth opportunities including silicon, optics, security and AI.

catalysts.claim: Cisco's full-year revenue guidance is $74.8 billion to $75.8 billion.

recent_developments.claim: In the first quarter, total revenue was $18.5 billion, up 24%, with product revenue up 32% and services revenue up 1%.
recent_developments.quote: Revenue -- Total revenue was $18.5 billion, up 24%, with product revenue up 32% and services revenue up 1%.

recent_developments.claim: Networking product revenue grew 43% in the quarter, well ahead of Security at 7%, Collaboration at 8% and Observability at 2%.
recent_developments.quote: Product revenue performance reflected growth in Networking up 43%, Security up 7%, Collaboration up 8%, and Observability up 2%.

recent_developments.claim: GAAP total gross margin fell to 63.7% from 65.5% a year earlier, and product gross margin fell to 61.8% from 64.5%.
recent_developments.quote: On a GAAP basis, total gross margin, product gross margin, and services gross margin were 63.7%, 61.8%, and 70.9%, respectively, as compared with 65.5%, 64.5%, and 68.4%, respectively, in the first quarter of fiscal 2026.

recent_developments.claim: Inventories rose to $5.7 billion from $3.2 billion, reflecting higher demand for Cisco Silicon One and higher memory prices.
recent_developments.quote: Inventories were $5.7 billion as of July 25, 2026 compared with $3.2 billion as of July 26, 2025, reflecting increased demand for our Cisco Silicon One and the impact of higher memory prices.

insight.claim: At the end of the fiscal year, Cisco's inventory was up 80% and its inventory purchase commitments with contract manufacturers and suppliers were up 126%.
insight.source: 10-K, Item 7 MD&A, Liquidity and Capital Resources, Inventory Supply Chain
insight.line: Inventory as of July 25, 2026 increased by 80% and inventory purchase commitments with contract manufacturers and suppliers increased by 126% from our balances at the end of fiscal 2025.

financial_analyst.statement_analysis:
### Cisco Systems, Inc. (CSCO), fiscal year ended 2026-07-25 (FY2026)
All FY2026 and FY2025 facts come from 10-K 0000858877-26-000132, filed 2026-09-02. Amounts are in $ millions, except per share. Every ratio below was computed in code.

**Growth (FY2026 vs FY2025)**
- Total revenue was **$63,325.0 million**, against **$56,654.0 million** a year earlier.
  - Source: us-gaap:RevenueFromContractWithCustomerExcludingAssessedTax, periods 2025-07-27 to 2026-07-25 and 2024-07-28 to 2025-07-26.
  - Revenue growth was **11.77%** = 63,325.0 / 56,654.0 - 1.
- Operating income was **$15,368.0 million**, against **$11,760.0 million**.
  - Source: us-gaap:OperatingIncomeLoss, same periods.
  - Operating income growth was **30.68%** = 15,368.0 / 11,760.0 - 1.
- Net income attributable to Cisco was **$13,267.0 million**, against **$10,180.0 million**.
  - Source: us-gaap:NetIncomeLoss, same periods.
  - Net income growth was **30.32%** = 13,267.0 / 10,180.0 - 1.
- GAAP diluted EPS was **$3.33**, against **$2.55**.
  - Source: us-gaap:EarningsPerShareDiluted, same periods.
  - Diluted EPS growth was **30.59%** = 3.33 / 2.55 - 1.
- Profits grew much faster than revenue.

**Margins**
- Operating margin was **24.27%** = 15,368.0 / 63,325.0. The prior year was **20.76%** = 11,760.0 / 56,654.0.
- Net margin was **20.95%** = 13,267.0 / 63,325.0. The prior year was **17.97%** = 10,180.0 / 56,654.0.
- Both margins widened year over year.

**Returns on equity**
- Stockholders' equity was **$50,285.0 million** at 2026-07-25 and **$46,843.0 million** at 2025-07-26.
  - Source: us-gaap:StockholdersEquity.
- Return on average equity was **27.32%** = 13,267.0 / ((50,285.0 + 46,843.0) / 2).
- ROE on year-end equity has been requested from the calculator. It is not computed here.

**Leverage**
- At 2026-07-25:
  - Long-term debt (noncurrent) was **$19,372.0 million** (us-gaap:LongTermDebtNoncurrent).
  - The current portion of long-term debt was **$3,500.0 million** (us-gaap:LongTermDebtCurrent).
- At 2025-07-26, the same two lines were **$22,861.0 million** and **$1,750.0 million**.
- Debt to equity was **0.455** = (19,372.0 + 3,500.0) / 50,285.0.
- The prior year was **0.525** = (22,861.0 + 1,750.0) / 46,843.0.
- Leverage fell.

**Cash flow**
- Cash from operations was **$14,177.0 million**, against **$14,193.0 million**.
  - Source: us-gaap:NetCashProvidedByUsedInOperatingActivities.
  - Growth was **-0.11%** = 14,177.0 / 14,193.0 - 1.
- Additions to property and equipment were **$1,410.0 million**, against **$905.0 million**.
  - Source: us-gaap:PaymentsToAcquirePropertyPlantAndEquipment.
  - Growth was **55.80%** = 1,410.0 / 905.0 - 1.
- Free cash flow was **$12,767.0M** = 14,177.0 - 1,410.0.
  - The prior year was **$13,288.0M** = 14,193.0 - 905.0.
  - Free cash flow growth was **-3.92%** = (14,177.0 - 1,410.0) / (14,193.0 - 905.0) - 1.
- Free cash flow margin was **20.16%** = (14,177.0 - 1,410.0) / 63,325.0.
- Free cash flow / net income was **0.96** = (14,177.0 - 1,410.0) / 13,267.0.
- Cash generation was flat while earnings rose about 30%. Free cash flow fell slightly as capital spending stepped up.
financial_analyst.latest_quarter:
### Q1 FY2027: three months ended October 24, 2026
**Source:** 8-K accession 0000858877-26-000170, Item 2.02, Exhibit 99.1, accepted 2026-11-12 16:06:24 ET. The figures are in millions, except per-share amounts.

**Revenue**
- Release line: `Total revenue | 18,517 | 14,883`. The columns are October 24, 2026 and October 25, 2025.
- Revenue growth on the same quarter last year was **24.42%** = 18,517 / 14,883 - 1, computed in code.
- The release rounds this to "Increase of 24% year over year".

**GAAP diluted EPS**
- Under the heading "Net income per share:", the release line is `Diluted | $1.14 | $0.72`.
- Diluted EPS growth on the same quarter last year was **58.33%** = 1.14 / 0.72 - 1, computed in code.
- The release states: `Diluted Earnings per Share (EPS) | $1.14 | $0.72 | 58%`.

**Other release figures**
- The release summary gives operating margin as "GAAP: 30.2%; Non-GAAP: 37.8%".
- It gives non-GAAP EPS of $1.40. That figure is reported here only for reference; this analysis uses GAAP.
- The GAAP operating margin is above the FY2026 level of 24.27%. The two periods differ: one is a quarter and one is a full year.

financial_analyst.valuation:
**P/E: 30.6** = 102.01 / 3.33 (price / GAAP diluted EPS).

**Inputs**
- **Price:** $102.01, the close of 2026-11-12. This was the last close before the release was accepted at 2026-11-12 16:06:24 ET. Source: financialdatasets.ai.
- **EPS:** $3.33, FY2026 GAAP diluted EPS. Source: us-gaap:EarningsPerShareDiluted, 2025-07-27 to 2026-07-25, 10-K 0000858877-26-000132.
- This P/E is on fiscal-year GAAP EPS. It is not on trailing twelve months that include Q1 FY2027.

**What the ratios say about value**
- The multiple of 30.6 sits against:
  - FY2026 diluted EPS growth of 30.59%.
  - Q1 FY2027 GAAP diluted EPS growth of 58.33% (release: $1.14 vs $0.72).
  - Return on average equity of 27.32%.
  - Debt to equity falling to 0.455.
- Free cash flow did not keep pace with earnings:
  - Free cash flow was $12,767.0M, down 3.92%.
  - Free cash flow / net income was 0.96.
- No peer multiples are in context, so no relative valuation can be stated.
definitions: Revenue is total revenue as tagged us-gaap:RevenueFromContractWithCustomerExcludingAssessedTax in the 10-K, and the release's 'Total revenue' line for the quarter.
Return on equity uses average stockholders' equity of the FY2026 and FY2025 year-ends, (50,285.0 + 46,843.0) / 2; year-end ROE was requested from the calculator, not computed.
EPS is GAAP diluted EPS (us-gaap:EarningsPerShareDiluted; the release's 'Diluted' line), not the release's non-GAAP EPS of $1.40.
Net income is net income attributable to the parent (us-gaap:NetIncomeLoss).
Debt is long-term debt noncurrent plus current maturities of long-term debt; debt to equity uses year-end stockholders' equity.
Free cash flow is cash from operations minus additions to property and equipment (us-gaap:PaymentsToAcquirePropertyPlantAndEquipment).
P/E uses the 2026-11-12 close of $102.01 over FY2026 GAAP diluted EPS of $3.33.

insight.claim: Free cash flow did not keep up with earnings in FY2026. Additions to property and equipment rose 55.80% to $1,410.0 million while cash from operations was essentially flat at $14,177.0 million (-0.11%), so free cash flow fell 3.92% to $12,767.0M even as net income grew 30.32%.
insight.source: 10-K 0000858877-26-000132, filed 2026-09-02, consolidated statements of cash flows
insight.line: us-gaap:PaymentsToAcquirePropertyPlantAndEquipment, 2025-07-27 to 2026-07-25 ($1,410.0 million; prior $905.0 million), and us-gaap:NetCashProvidedByUsedInOperatingActivities, 2025-07-27 to 2026-07-25 ($14,177.0 million; prior $14,193.0 million)

deciding_number.label: Free cash flow growth, FY2026 vs FY2025

output.thesis: Cisco's earnings are accelerating. FY2026 GAAP diluted EPS grew **30.59%** to $3.33, and Q1 FY2027 GAAP diluted EPS grew **58.33%** on revenue up **24.42%**, led by Networking up 43% and hyperscaler AI demand that management now expects to reach $9B in FY27. At a **P/E of 30.6**, however, the stock already prices in roughly the FY2026 rate of EPS growth. Cash has not followed earnings: free cash flow fell **3.92%** to **$12,767.0M** while net income grew **30.32%**, because cash from operations was flat (**-0.11%**) and additions to property and equipment rose **55.80%**. The balance sheet is also absorbing the AI build-out: inventory rose 80%, inventory purchase commitments rose 126%, and Q1 GAAP product gross margin fell to 61.8% from 64.5%. Strong returns (return on average equity of **27.32%**) and falling leverage (debt to equity of **0.455**) limit the downside, so the case is Hold rather than Sell.
output.what_would_change_it: We would move to Buy if free cash flow starts growing with earnings, which would show that the inventory build is converting to cash at a steady gross margin. We would move to Sell if inventory and purchase commitments keep rising while gross margin keeps falling below the Q1 GAAP level of 63.7%.
strategic_recommendations: Watch whether inventory of $5.7 billion, up from $3.2 billion, starts converting to operating cash. FY2026 cash from operations was flat at $14,177.0 million, and that conversion is the main test of earnings quality.

Track GAAP total gross margin against the Q1 level of 63.7%, which was down from 65.5%. Management attributes part of the pressure to higher memory prices, and the filing notes continuing price-focused competition from China.

Measure progress against the raised expectation of $9B in hyperscaler AI infrastructure revenue for FY27 and the revenue guidance of $74.8 billion - $75.8 billion. The filing itself flags customer concentration and supply considerations tied to that demand.

insight.claim: At the end of FY2026, Cisco's inventory was up 80% and its inventory purchase commitments with contract manufacturers and suppliers were up 126%, which signals a large forward supply build behind the AI demand that the release's first paragraph does not mention.
insight.source: 10-K, Item 7 MD&A, Liquidity and Capital Resources, Inventory Supply Chain
insight.line: Inventory as of July 25, 2026 increased by 80% and inventory purchase commitments with contract manufacturers and suppliers increased by 126% from our balances at the end of fiscal 2025.
